newsitem.title: USA: Former AT&T employee settles inside trade suit.
newsitem.headline: Former AT&T employee settles inside trade suit.

text.p: Two men, one a former employee of AT&T Corp, agreed to pay penalties to settle civil charges they violated federal securities laws in connection with an insider trading scheme on stocks of AT&T takeover targets.

Thomas Alger, a former employee in AT&T's human resources department and William Mylett, agreed to the settlement without admitting or denying allegations, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Tuesday.
Alger agreed to pay $204,851 which includes disgorgement of his profits, prejudgment interest and a civil penalty.

Mylett, who allegedly traded on the information, had $600,147 in penalities plus prejudgment interest levied against him. But because of his inability to pay, all but $68,000 was waived, the SEC said.

Alger and Mylett were both permanently enjoined from violationg federal securities laws in the future, the SEC said. Both men had also pleaded guilty earlier to separate criminal charges, including conspiracy to commit securities fraud.
SEC charged Alger in February 1995 for allegedly orchestrating trading of stocks of four AT&T targets: NCR Corp, Digital Microwave Corp, Paradyne Corp and Teradata Corp.
Alger and Charles Brumfield, also a former AT&T executive allegedly gave "tips" to others who traded on the information. Brumfield had agreed last month to pay $813,600 in penalities.
A total of 17 persons have been charged in this case by the SEC. Litigation against the remaining defendants is continuing.
